Subject: Medisync redlines + clarification on training/use of outputs

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Attached are Medisync's consolidated redlines to the MSA and the draft order form (Medisync_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf, OrderForm_Medisync_v2.xlsx). Two asks up front so we can scope procurement and legal review:

1) Output ownership: our product team needs the right to commercialize outputs generated by Medisync customer prompts (we lean to assignment for productization). We flagged specific paragraphs in the MSA.
2) Training/feedback: we are concerned about a broad feedback license. We need a clear carveout for any prompts and data that include PHI or other proprietary training sets unless we explicitly opt in.

Can your legal team propose language that separates (a) outputs we productize from (b) aggregated model improvements Redwood may use? Also please confirm whether choosing Dedicated or Private deployment changes the default rights you propose.

We'd like a short call Thursday 21st 10:00-10:30 PT to walk legal and procurement through the suggested path and any pricing impact. 

Thanks,
Anika Shah
Sr. Head of Product, Medisync
Anika Shah <anika@medisync.com>

Subject: Re: Medisync redlines + clarification on training/use of outputs

Anika —

Appreciate the redlines and clear asks. Short answers up front:
- We can propose a split approach that gives Medisync broad commercial rights to outputs you productize while preserving a narrowly scoped feedback license for Redwood to improve models (with explicit PHI/proprietary-data carveouts).
- Dedicated or Private deployment materially changes the options: Private/Dedicated allows you to exclude feedback telemetry and opt out of training use entirely (ops/infra/control + pricing delta).

I'm looping in Laura (legal) and Monica (customer success/ops) to draft an MSA excerpt and a recommended Order Form amendment that maps rights to deployment choices and price buckets.

Call confirmed for Thu 21st 10:00 PT — invite coming from my calendar.

Next steps from Redwood: Laura will send two alternative clauses (one for hosted with a narrow feedback license, one for Dedicated/Private that preserves customer-only use). We'll also attach a revised order form showing the Dedicated/Private pricing uplift.

Talk soon,

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft language for training/feedback carveouts and output rights (MSA excerpt)

Anika / Rishi —

Following our quick sync, attached is a focused excerpt (MSA_excerpt_training_clause.docx) with two alternative pathways. Key points below and rationale for legal review: 

Option A — Hosted (default):
- Customer owns outputs they generate.
- Redwood receives a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable, limited feedback license to use Customer-provided prompts and non-PHI telemetry in aggregate and anonymized form solely to improve Redwood services and models.
- Explicit carveout: any data identified by Customer as PHI, PII, or otherwise marked proprietary is excluded from the feedback license and will not be used for model training without Customer's express opt-in.

Option B — Dedicated / Private (procurement path):
- Customer continues to own outputs.
- No feedback license granted to Redwood by default; Redwood will not use any customer data or telemetry for model training or improvements unless expressly contracted and compensated.
- Price uplift and operational controls (VPC, KMS integration, longer retention windows) are included.

Productization / Assignment ask: Medisync requested assignment of outputs for productization. Our commercial compromise is: 
- For outputs generated solely from Customer-provided proprietary training sets (i.e., content supplied offline by Customer and explicitly identified as such), Customer may receive exclusive rights for productization if Customer contracts for Private deployment or an enhanced Dedicated tier and agrees to the corresponding pricing and SLA.
- For outputs created from general prompts on hosted tiers, Redwood offers a broad perpetual license to Customer to use, distribute, and sublicense outputs but cannot accept wholesale assignment of model-level IP.

Operational notes:
- We can add an opt-out checkbox and an Evidence Request annex for customers that require proof of non-use.
- We recommend a brief commissioning clause for attorneys to sign off on the exact PHI/PII markers and processes.

If this framework works, I'll prepare redline text for the MSA and a short Order Form amendment mapping the choices to price buckets.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: MSA_excerpt_training_clause.docx (docx)

Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft language for training/feedback carveouts and output rights (MSA excerpt)

Laura / Rishi —

Thanks, that structure is helpful and much clearer than the previous draft. A few follow-ups from product and legal here at Medisync: 

1) The distinction in the Productization / Assignment section still feels like it could be gamed. We need the exclusive productization right to apply to outputs produced by models trained substantially on Medisync-supplied datasets, not merely "proprietary prompts." Can you propose a definition for "substantially trained on"?

2) Regarding Hosted tier outputs: we prefer assignment for outputs we pay to generate at scale (commercial feature runs). If Hosted remains a license, please outline clear limitations on Redwood's re-use (for example, no direct resale of customer prompts/outputs, no use to build a competing vertical model).

3) Evidence request: we will want a stronger audit clause or telemetry attestation if you claim Dedicated/Private prevents use for training. Can you include a simple quarterly certification and a right to audit under NDA?

Also please confirm pricing impact for Exclusive Productization (approx. ballpark uplift %) so procurement can prepare the internal approval.

Proposed call to close redlines: Thu 23 May 11:00 - 11:30 PT?

-Anika
Sr. Head of Product, Medisync

Subject: Proposed path forward and updated order form (summary)

Anika / team —

Thanks for the thorough feedback over the week. Summary of agreed commercial/legal path and immediate next steps: 

1) Definitions: Laura will propose a narrow, measurable definition for "substantially trained on" (suggestion: >60% of training dataset tokens are derived from Customer-supplied corpora + documented evidence of dataset provenance). That definition will be presented in the MSA redline by EOD Mon 27 May.

2) Hosted tier: Customer retains strong usage rights to outputs (unrestricted downstream use). Redwood will not resell customer prompts or outputs in a way that competes directly with Customer verticals. We will add explicit non-compete re-use language and a prohibition on building vertical product replicas using identifiable customer outputs.

3) Exclusive productization: Available only when Customer purchases Dedicated or Private deployment AND signs the Exclusive Productization Addendum. Pricing uplift for Exclusive Productization and the Private control plane will be shown in the attached OrderForm_Medisync_v2.xlsx (highlighted column). Ballpark uplift for Exclusive productization + Private: mid-to-high single-digit percentage on top of the Dedicated/Private base; exact numbers to be finalized by Finance.

4) Evidence & audit: Redwood will agree to a quarterly attestation that no customer-marked PHI/PII was used for training and provide a limited right to audit under NDA for Dedicated/Private customers. The attestation template will be appended as an annex.

5) Next actions:
- Laura to send final redline MSA and Exclusive Productization Addendum (target: Mon 27 May).
- Rishi to update HubSpot deal HLT-2029-0342 and circulate revised Order Form for procurement signatures.
- Monica to schedule a procurement handoff with your finance team and provide a procurement checklist.

If this matches your view, I'll issue the DocuSign package Tuesday and we can aim for signed order form by end of next week.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
